arxiv-2103-13784.creator: Mogens Fosgerau, Mads Paulsen, Thomas Kjær Rasmussen
arxiv-2103-13784.description: Abstract We propose a route choice model in which traveler behavior is represented as a utility maximizing assignment of flow across an entire network under a flow conservation constraint . Substitution between routes depends on how much they overlap. The model is estimated considering the full set of route alternatives, and no choice set generation is required.

arxiv-2106-10094.title: A Categorical Construction of the Real Unit Interval
arxiv-2106-10094.creator: John van de Wetering
arxiv-2106-10094.description: Abstract The real unit interval is the fundamental building block for many branches of mathematics like probability theory, measure theory, convex sets and homotopy theory. However, a priori the unit interval could be considered an arbitrary choice and one can wonder if there is some more canonical way in which the unit interval can be constructed.

arxiv-2208-11874.title: Is magic texture for Majorana neutrino immanent in Dirac nature?
arxiv-2208-11874.creator: Yuta Hyodo, Teruyuki Kitabayashi
arxiv-2208-11874.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuta Hyodo, Teruyuki Kitabayashi. The magic textures are successful candidates of the correct texture for the Majorana neutrinos. In this study, we show that some types of magic texture for Majorana neutrinos approximately immanent in the flavor mass matrix for Dirac neutrinos. In addition, it turned out that the normal mass ordering of the Dirac neutrino masses is slightly preferable to the inverted mass ordering in the context of the magic textures. 1 Introduction Are neutrinos Majorana or Dirac particles?

pmc-11348038.title: Head Nurse Leadership: Facilitators and Barriers to Adherence to Infection Prevention and Control Programs—A Qualitative Study Protocol †
pmc-11348038.creator: Eva Cappelli, Jacopo Fiorini, Francesco Zaghini, Federica Canzan, Alessandro Sili, Richard Gray
pmc-11348038.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The effective management of Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) relies on the implementation of good practice across the entire multidisciplinary team. The organizational context and the role of head nurses influence the team’s performance and behavior. Understanding how decision-making processes influence healthcare professionals’ behavior in the management of HAIs could help identify alternative interventions for reducing the risk of infection in healthcare organizations.

pmc-11354071.title: Different Nitrogen Consumption Patterns in Low Temperature Fermentations in the Wine Yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae
pmc-11354071.creator: Estéfani García-Ríos, Judit Pardo, Ying Su, José Manuel Guillamón, Gino Ciafardini
pmc-11354071.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Nowadays, the wine industry carries out fermentations at low temperatures because this oenological practice clearly improves the aromatic complexity of the final wines. In addition, nitrogen content of the must also influences the quality of the wine. In this study, we carried out a phenotypic and fermentative analysis of two industrial wine Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains (P5 and P24) at 15 and 28 °C and three nitrogen concentrations (60, 140 and 300 mg N/L) in synthetic must.

pmc-11415815.title: The application of untargeted metabolomics coupled with chemometrics for the analysis of agitation effects on the sensory profiles of matcha tea
pmc-11415815.creator: Siying Li, Hehe Tian, Guilong Zhu, Zhenbo Wei
pmc-11415815.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In the study, the effects of agitating parameters (different agitating rates and time) on the aroma and taste profiles of matcha tea were systematically investigated by the combination of untargeted metabolomics and chemometrics. The aroma profiles of matcha tea agitated at low rates (500 rpm) and for 30 s were more richness than that agitated with other parameters by sensory analysis and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry.

pmc-11484307.title: Metal-organic-framework-based sitagliptin-release platform for multieffective radiation-induced intestinal injury targeting therapy and intestinal flora protective capabilities
pmc-11484307.creator: Dan He, ZhiHui Li, Min Wang, Dejun Kong, Wenyan Guo, Xuliang Xia, Dong Li, Daijun Zhou
pmc-11484307.description: In patients with abdominal or pelvic tumors, radiotherapy can result in radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII), a potentially severe complication for which there are few effective therapeutic options. Sitagliptin (SI) is an oral hypoglycemic drug that exhibits antiapoptotic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory activity, but how it influences RIII-associated outcomes has yet to be established.

pmc-11521235.title: Genetic Markers of Spina Bifida in an Indian Cohort
pmc-11521235.creator: Prabudh Goel, Mahima Sharma, Himani Kaushik, Sourabh Kumar, Harpreet Singh, Vishesh Jain, Anjan Kumar Dhua, Devendra Kumar Yadav, Neeta Kumar, Sandeep Agarwala
pmc-11521235.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective:To identify the genetic markers of spina bifida through a systematic survey of the exome in an Indian cohort.Materials and Methods:Three consecutive patients (P1: 1 year, male; P2: 2.8 years, male; and P3: 10 years, female) with spina bifida (lumbosacral meningomyelocele) underwent whole-exome sequencing (libraries: SureSelect Human All Exon V8; sequencing: 2 * 150 bp paired-end run, 100×) with NovaSeq 6000.

pmc-11607317.title: Habitual physical activity is related to more creative activities and achievements
pmc-11607317.creator: Christian Rominger, Andreas Fink, Corinna M. Perchtold-Stefan, Mathias Benedek, Andreas R. Schwerdtfeger
pmc-11607317.description: Beyond health, physical activity (PA) is associated with better creative ideation performance. People who are habitually more physically active produce more original ideas when asked to think creatively about an alternative use of an everyday object such as a brick.

pmc-12973028.title: Indigenous Innovation in Orthopedic Robotics: Making Joint Replacement Affordable in India
pmc-12973028.creator: Kunal Aneja, Ponnanna Karineravanda Machaiah, Ashok Shyam
pmc-12973028.description: Robotic-assisted joint replacement has transformed contemporary arthroplasty by improving surgical precision, implant positioning, and soft-tissue balancing, with emerging evidence suggesting benefits in early functional recovery and alignment accuracy. Despite these advantages, the widespread adoption of orthopaedic robotics in India remains constrained by high capital investment, recurring maintenance costs, limited insurance reimbursement, and restricted access to structured training.

pmc-13222772.title: Integrating Existential Perspectives into Schema Therapy: A Conceptual Framework with Clinical Illustrations
pmc-13222772.creator: Jan Prasko, Julija Gecaite-Stonciene, Marija Abeltina, Marie Ociskova, Jakub Vanek, Ilona Krone, Ieva Bite, Milos Slepecky, Alicja Juskiene
pmc-13222772.description: BackgroundExistential concerns such as meaninglessness, isolation, freedom, responsibility, and death anxiety represent core dimensions of human suffering and may underlie chronic psychological distress, particularly in patients with personality pathology. Although schema therapy implicitly addresses such themes, their systematic integration has remained conceptually underdeveloped.

pmc-13590066.creator: Jack Larsen, Patrick Kenney, Tonya Milam, Joyce Troxler, Caleb Osborne, Maria Zambrano
pmc-13590066.description: IntroductionBuprenorphine is internationally recognized as an effective treatment for Opioid Use Disorder (OUD). Pill counting, a quantitative assessment of medication supply to monitor prescription medication adherence, is often recommended to monitor buprenorphine adherence. However, there is little evidence to support pill counting or examine its impact on addiction treatment.
